issues.legal_issue: The term “entertained” in a restriction on applications to set aside an execution sale means consideration on the merits, so a compliance condition in force when the court considers the application applies even if the application was filed before the condition was added.
material_facts: An application to set aside an execution sale was filed before a deposit-or-security condition was added to the applicable procedural rule.
The application was considered after the condition had been added, and the applicant had not deposited security.
The High Court dismissed the appeal because the applicant had not complied with the added condition.
issues.conclusion: The added condition applied to the pending application because “entertained” means adjudicated or proceeded with on the merits, not initiated.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 21, Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure, as amended, “entertained” means adjudicate upon or proceed to consider on the merits. The Court followed Lakshmi-ratan Engineering Works Ltd. v. Assistant Commissioner, Sales Tax, Kanpur, which accepted that interpretation, and referred to the Allahabad High Court decisions in Kundan Lal v. Jagan Nath Sharma, Dhoom Chand Jain v. Chaman-lal Gupta, Haji Rahim Bux and Sons v. Firm Samiullah and Sons, and Mahavir Singh v. Gauri Shankar.

predicates.sale_setting_application: A party applies to set aside a sale conducted to enforce a judgment.
predicates.condition_added_after_filing: A compliance condition is added to the governing procedure after the application is filed.
predicates.application_considered_on_merits: The court takes up the application for consideration on its merits.

issues.definition: When an application to set aside an enforcement sale is considered on its merits after a compliance condition is added, that condition applies even though the application was filed earlier.

issues.legal_issue: A court has discretion over the amount and requirement of a deposit or security for an application to set aside an execution sale and should ordinarily give the applicant an opportunity to comply, particularly when the application predates the condition and the parties proceeded as though it did not apply.
material_facts: The application to set aside the sale was filed several months before the deposit-or-security condition was added.
The parties proceeded before the executing court on the basis that the new condition did not apply, and the court did not call on the applicant to provide security.
The compliance objection was raised for the first time in the High Court.

The High Court refused the applicant’s request for an opportunity to comply, treating compliance as mandatory and beyond the court’s power to permit after the application had been considered on the merits.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should have remitted the matter to the executing court to exercise its discretion concerning compliance; the appeal was allowed and the case remitted.
issues.legal_principle: Order 21, Rule 90’s amended proviso gives the court discretion to determine the amount of the deposit or security, subject to the prescribed maximum, and to dispense with the requirement for recorded reasons. The court ordinarily should give the applicant an opportunity to comply and may reject the application if the applicant still does not comply. The Court relied on the interpretation in Kundan Lal v. Jagan Nath Sharma and held that this approach was particularly appropriate where the application predated the added condition and the parties had proceeded on the assumption that it did not apply.

rule.if: execution_sale_challenge and application_predates_compliance_condition and parties_proceeded_without_compliance and court_did_not_seek_compliance

predicates.execution_sale_challenge: A party challenges a sale conducted to enforce a judgment.
predicates.application_predates_compliance_conditio: The application was filed before a compliance condition was added to the governing procedure.
predicates.parties_proceeded_without_compliance: The parties conducted the proceedings on the understanding that the added condition did not apply.
predicates.court_did_not_seek_compliance: The court did not call on the applicant to comply before the compliance objection was raised.

issues.definition: When a challenge to an enforcement sale was filed before a compliance condition was added, the parties proceeded without compliance, and the court did not seek compliance, the matter should be remitted for a discretionary compliance decision.
